one_line: Nvidia reports strong quarterly revenue while facing executive changes, export controls, and congressional testimony, alongside major model releases from OpenAI and Microsoft.

themes.title: Nvidia reports record earnings amid leadership and export sh
themes.text: Nvidia posted $115.8 billion in third-quarter revenue and stopped reporting its Singapore unit revenue after it hit $104 billion. Meanwhile, the company ended H200 chip sales to China, its board stated it will not reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang ahead of his congressional testimony, and the U.S. issued new export controls targeting data centers in Southeast Asia.

stories.headline: Nvidia reports Q3 revenue of $115.8B and forecasts Q4 revenue of $130B
Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore unit revenue in 2025 as it hit $104B
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to testify before US House committees on Dec 1
Nvidia board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
Nvidia ends H200 chip sales in China under acting CEO Colette Kress
US Commerce Dept and DOJ investigated Megaspeed over chip exports in 2024
Nvidia board creates National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee
US tightens AI chip export rules, targeting Southeast Asia data centres

themes.title: New model releases from major labs
themes.text: OpenAI launched its GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models with lower pricing and benchmark gains, while Microsoft unveiled six new models including MAI Code 2. Additionally, Anthropic reported porting its Claude Mythos Preview model to AMD GPUs in three days with minimal human intervention.

stories.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol for ChatGPT Work and Codex
OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models with benchmark gains
Microsoft unveils six AI models including MAI Code 2 and Flash
Anthropic says Claude Mythos ported to AMD GPUs in three days with almost no human work

themes.title: Funding rounds and infrastructure developments
themes.text: Isomorphic Labs raised $5 billion in Series C funding for its drug-design engine, and Paris-based robot maker Genesis AI secured a $500 million Series A. Numa raised $45 million for its dealership operating system, while Amazon's $17 billion Ohio data center plans faced setbacks following local voter restrictions.

stories.headline: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion Series C to speed AI‑driven drug trials
Genesis AI raises $500 million Series A at $3.5 billion valuation
Numa raises $45M Series C to expand AI operating system for car dealerships
Amazon's Ohio data center plans face risks after voter restrictions
